name: Teej
description: A monsoon festival welcoming the rains, when women in green swing on decorated jhoolas, apply henna and celebrate with processions of the goddess Parvati.

name: Pushkar Camel Fair
description: One of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs, combining trade with folk music, competitions and a sacred lake pilgrimage.

name: Baisakhi
description: The harvest festival and Sikh new year marking the founding of the Khalsa in 1699, celebrated with bhangra, giddha and gurdwara processions.

name: Hola Mohalla
description: A Sikh festival of martial arts, mock battles and Nihang horsemanship held at Anandpur Sahib.

name: Dev Deepawali
description: The 'Diwali of the Gods' in Varanasi, when the ghats are lit with hundreds of thousands of earthen lamps.

name: Ram Navami
description: The birth of Lord Rama, celebrated with special fervour in Ayodhya with processions and recitations of the Ramayana.

name: Chhath Puja
description: A four-day festival of thanksgiving to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, when devotees stand in rivers at dawn and dusk offering arghya — Bihar's most important festival.

name: Buddha Purnima
description: The birth, enlightenment and death of the Buddha, observed at Bodh Gaya with prayer, meditation and processions.

name: Phoolwalon Ki Sair
description: A centuries-old Delhi procession of flower-sellers celebrating communal harmony, offering floral fans at a temple and a dargah.

name: Qutub Festival
description: A cultural festival of classical music and dance staged against the backdrop of the Qutub Minar (demo: schedule varies year to year).
